# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# scenario: --scenario failed.
# NOT IN DESIGN.md §8's deliverable list; added by Phase 0 with its reason recorded in
# decisions/phase0-mock.md and tests/fixtures/README.md ("Additions"). The reason: §2a.4 names the
# test "the mock answers get_transfer_by_txid with a FAILED-type row and the test asserts the next
# send exits 0 with an empty record", and --fail cannot produce it: --fail yields a JSON-RPC ERROR,
# while this case is a SUCCESSFUL response whose `type` happens to be "failed". --scenario is the
# mechanism DESIGN.md §8 provides for a second fixture of one method.
# fields: identical to get_transfer_by_txid.json -- COMMAND_RPC_GET_TRANSFER_BY_TXID::response_t,
#         src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:1667-1676; transfer_entry :1446-1487.
# WHY THE CASE EXISTS AT ALL: on_get_transfer_by_txid searches get_unconfirmed_payments_out
#         (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:3014-3022), the same source that feeds BOTH the `pending`
#         and the `failed` lists of on_get_transfers, and fill_transfer_entry types those rows
#         `is_failed ? "failed" : "pending"` (:561). So a failed transaction IS findable by txid.
# WHY IT MUST COUNT AS FOUND (§2a.4): a `failed` row means the wallet saw the transaction and it did
#         not make it, which is not a double-spend risk. Treating it as not-found would leave the
#         pending.json record in place forever and force the user to type `clear-pending` out of
#         habit -- the one thing §2a.4 exists to prevent, because a habitual clear-pending disarms
#         the interlock that stops a double send.
# ONLY A POSITIVE "NOT FOUND" MAY BLOCK: that is -8 with the message "Transaction not found."
#         (:3045-3046) -> Ok(None) (§5b), reachable from the mock with
#         --fail get_transfer_by_txid=-8:'Transaction not found.'
# THE TXID is the same one as get_transfer_by_txid.json, transfer-do-not-relay.json and
#         relay_tx.json: this is the SAME transaction, seen after it failed rather than after it was
#         accepted. Only `type` differs. `locked` stays true, as it is unconditionally for
#         pending/failed rows (:551), and confirmations stays 0 because height is 0.
